definitions.explanation: An individual item or point in a list, document, or set of rules. Most commonly seen in the compound {箇条書|かじょうが}き (bullet-point list).

examples.japanese: ⟦{箇条書|かじょうが}き→箇条書き：16989_kajougaki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦まとめる→まとめる：02424_matomeru⟧。
⟦{要点|ようてん}→要点：01668_youten⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{箇条書|かじょうが}き→箇条書き：16989_kajougaki⟧にして⟦{提出|ていしゅつ}して→提出する：19644_teishutsusuru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please list the key points in bullet form and submit them.

examples.japanese: {五箇条|ごかじょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{御誓文|ごせいもん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{明治|めいじ}→明治：19860_meiji⟧⟦{政府|せいふ}→政府：03294_seifu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{基本方針|きほんほうしん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}した→示す：01948_shimesu⟧⟦{文書|ぶんしょ}→文書：12947_bunsho⟧だ。
examples.english: The Charter Oath of Five Articles was a document setting out the basic policies of the Meiji government.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in the compound ⟦{箇条書|かじょうが}き→箇条書き：16989_kajougaki⟧ (writing in listed items, bullet points), which is an essential word for business and academic Japanese. Also appears in historical terms like {五箇条|ごかじょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{御誓文|ごせいもん} (Charter Oath of Five Articles, 1868).

WRITING:
Also written {ヶ条|かじょう} or ⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧{条|じょう}. The {箇|か} kanji is sometimes replaced with the smaller ヶ.

WATCH OUT:
Not to be confused with ⟦{過剰|かじょう}→過剰：04123_kajou⟧ (excess, surplus).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{箇条書|かじょうが}き→箇条書き：16989_kajougaki⟧: bullet-point list
- {五箇条|ごかじょう}: five articles
- {数箇条|すうかじょう}: several items/articles
